content: Hi, I'm a new member, experimental subatomic physics in Manitoba Canada working on QCD and EW observables using the Electron-Ion Collider. Most of my day to day is event generators, simulation, event reconstruction algorithms, and connecting experimental observables to underlying physical quantities in methodologically sound ways, with a healthy dose of AI platform development in support of 1000+ member collaborations. I came here by way of PhysLib, primarily with the goal of contributing to a digitalized knowledge base of our subfield, with provable relationships. In particular, the impetus was an instance where genAI suggested that a specific coordinate transformation would computationally simplify an established jet clustering algorithm but was unable to provide a proof without essentially writing the full derivation and me checking it painstakingly. If AI is going to suggest results, I'd rather it do it in a provably correct way.

Your job sounds perfectly awesome!

I did environmental TEM with one of the world's best setups in Copenhagen and I got to play with the MAX IV synchrotron in Lund during my undergrad, but I would have loved to see some subatomics. That must be a blast!
